a month, a few thousand requests a day. On its own each tier is a toy. Stacked together, they add up to roughly \u003cstrong\u003e4 billion tokens per month\u003c/strong\u003e of working inference capacity, across \u003cstrong\u003e235 model families / 339 provider endpoints\u003c/strong\u003e from small-and-fast to reasonably capable.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe problem is that stacking them by hand is painful: twenty-eight different SDKs, twenty-eight different rate limits, twenty-eight places a request can fail. FreeLLMAPI collapses that into one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Point any OpenAI client library at your local server, and it routes transparently across whichever providers you've added keys for.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAnd the free-tier landscape shifts weekly: providers launch models, retire them, and change quotas without notice. FreeLLMAPI tracks all of that for you. The router pulls a signed model catalog from \u003ca href=\"https://freellmapi.co\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003efreellmapi.co\u003c/a\u003e on its own, so your install keeps up without a \u003ccode\u003egit pull\u003c/code\u003e. 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEvery OpenAI surface\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003e/v1/chat/completions\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e/v1/responses\u003c/code\u003e (what Codex CLI needs), \u003ccode\u003e/v1/completions\u003c/code\u003e (editor ghost-text autocomplete), \u003ccode\u003e/v1/images/generations\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e/v1/audio/speech\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e/v1/embeddings\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003e/v1/models\u003c/code\u003e — streaming and non-streaming, from the official SDKs or any OpenAI-compatible client. \u003ca href=\"/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/api.md\"\u003eAPI reference →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAnthropic Messages API\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003e/v1/messages\u003c/code\u003e speaks Anthropic's wire format over the same router, so \u003cstrong\u003eClaude Code\u003c/strong\u003e and the official Anthropic SDKs run against your free pool. \u003ca href=\"/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/api.md#anthropic--claude-clients\"\u003eDetails →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNative Gemini + Ollama surfaces\u003c/strong\u003e — Gemini CLI can use \u003ccode\u003e/v1beta\u003c/code\u003e (\u003ccode\u003egenerateContent\u003c/code\u003e, streaming, token counting, models), while opt-in Ollama emulation serves NDJSON chat/generate, tags, metadata, and embeddings for Zed, JetBrains, and other local-model clients.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFusion (multi-model synthesis)\u003c/strong\u003e — request the virtual \u003ccode\u003efusion\u003c/code\u003e model and the router fans your prompt out to a panel of diverse free models in parallel, then a judge model synthesizes one answer from the drafts. \u003ca href=\"/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/api.md#fusion-multi-model-synthesis\"\u003eDetails →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eImage generation \u0026amp; text-to-speech\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003e/v1/images/generations\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e/v1/audio/speech\u003c/code\u003e route across the providers that serve media models, including custom OpenAI-compatible media endpoints.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTool calling \u0026amp; structured outputs\u003c/strong\u003e — OpenAI-style \u003ccode\u003etools\u003c/code\u003e round-trip across providers (plain-text tool calls are rescued into real \u003ccode\u003etool_calls\u003c/code\u003e), plus \u003ccode\u003eresponse_format\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eseed\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elogprobs\u003c/code\u003e, penalties, and the rest of the sampling params passed through per provider.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSmart routing, six strategies\u003c/strong\u003e — live per-model speed/capability/reliability scores rank your chain; automatic fallover retries the next model on 429/5xx with cooldowns and key rotation. \u003ca href=\"/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#routing-in-detail\"\u003eRouting in detail →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUnified models \u0026amp; profiles\u003c/strong\u003e — the same model on several providers collapses into one entry with strict in-group failover; named fallback-chain profiles (a coding chain, a vision chain) switch from the dashboard or per request via \u003ccode\u003eauto:\u0026lt;profile\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePer-key rate tracking\u003c/strong\u003e — RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD counters per \u003ccode\u003e(platform, model, key)\u003c/code\u003e that learn providers' reported ceilings, so routing always stays under every cap.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSelf-updating model catalog\u003c/strong\u003e — the router syncs a signed catalog from freellmapi.co twice a day: new models, quota changes, and provider quirk fixes land automatically. \u003ca href=\"#premium-live-catalog\"\u003ePremium →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSticky sessions \u0026amp; context handoff\u003c/strong\u003e — conversations stay on one model for 30 minutes; an optional compact handoff note keeps the thread coherent when a mid-chat switch does happen. \u003ca href=\"/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/clients.md#context-handoff\"\u003eDetails →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePrompt compression (opt-in)\u003c/strong\u003e — a shared, fail-open request pipeline can deduplicate prompts, filter tool output, compact repeated JSON, and trim stale context before cache lookup and routing. \u003ca href=\"/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/compression.md\"\u003eDetails →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEncrypted keys, one token out\u003c/strong\u003e — provider keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted in SQLite and decrypted in-memory per request; your apps only ever see a single unified \u003ccode\u003efreellmapi-…\u003c/code\u003e bearer token.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAdmin dashboard \u0026amp; analytics\u003c/strong\u003e — React UI to manage keys, reorder the chain, run a playground, and read p50/p95/TTFT analytics over 24h–90d windows; login-gated, dark/light themes, \u003ca href=\"#languages\"\u003e60 languages\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMCP server \u0026amp; interactive docs\u003c/strong\u003e — agents can introspect usable models, provider health, and routing strategy over \u003ccode\u003e/mcp\u003c/code\u003e; a dependency-free OpenAPI viewer lives at \u003ccode\u003e/v1/docs\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ca href=\"/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/clients.md\"\u003eCoding agents →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOps niceties\u003c/strong\u003e — opt-in response cache, encrypted DB backups, periodic key health checks, bulk key import/export, declarative startup config. \u003ca href=\"/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/install.md\"\u003eInstall \u0026amp; deploy →\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRuns anywhere Node 20+ runs\u003c/strong\u003e — Windows, macOS, Linux servers, or a small ARM SBC (Raspberry Pi included). ~40 MB RSS at idle behind PM2 / systemd / whatever supervisor you prefer.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe scope is deliberately narrow — see \u003ca title="ci(desktop): fall back to unsigned DMG when Apple signing secrets are absent (#563)

* ci(desktop): fall back to an unsigned DMG when Apple signing secrets are absent

Tagged macOS release builds have hard-failed since the signing validation
landed (2026-06-27) because the repo has no Apple secrets configured — which
is why no DMG shipped after v0.4.1. With no cert at all, warn and build
unsigned (v0.4.1 behavior); a cert without notarization creds is still a
hard error, since that's a misconfiguration rather than a deliberate
unsigned release.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(desktop): unset empty signing env vars so unsigned builds don't fail

Unconfigured secrets arrive as empty env vars; electron-builder treats a
present-but-empty CSC_LINK as a certificate path and fails with 'not a
file' on every non-PR build (PR builds skip signing entirely, which is
why the smoke test stayed green while dispatch/tag builds broke).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

credential placement, quota boundaries, cooldown visibility (#597)

Seven fixes found by auditing the 156 forks that are ahead of main.

Credential handling:
- Send the Gemini key as an x-goog-api-key header instead of ?key= at all
  four call sites (chat, stream, validateKey, TTS in services/media.ts). The
  query form leaked the key into proxy access logs, browser history and any
  error string echoing the request URL. Verified live against the Gemini API:
  header authenticates, absent header returns 403.
- Redact credentials from every console writer, installed before anything
  logs. Distinct from lib/error-redaction.ts, which also strips URLs and
  truncates and so would make server logs unreadable. The one intentional
  disclosure — the unified API key printed at first boot — now writes
  straight to stdout so onboarding still works.

Quota accounting:
- Provider-account daily caps count from midnight UTC rather than a sliding
  24h window. Real caps (OpenRouter, NVIDIA) reset on a wall-clock day, so a
  burst at 23:00 kept a provider benched until 22:00 the next day.
- Clamp Retry-After to 24h. The parsed value feeds the cooldown expiry
  directly, so a malformed header (Retry-After: 99999999999) benched a key
  effectively forever.

Operability:
- Surface active cooldowns per key on GET /api/keys and add
  DELETE /api/keys/:id/cooldowns. An escalated cooldown can bench a key for
  24h while it still reads healthy and enabled, with no way back short of
  restarting and waiting.
- Set busy_timeout=5000 and chmod 0600 the SQLite file and its WAL sidecars.
  The dashboard and proxy write concurrently, and the DB holds encrypted
  provider keys plus the dashboard password hash.
- Call ensureModelInProfiles after the declarative-config chain insert.
  routes/keys.ts already did this; without it an env-configured model showed
  in the dashboard but was never routed once a profile was active.

Tests: 43 new cases across 6 files, plus Retry-After clamping in the existing
ratelimit suite. Each was confirmed to fail with its fix reverted. Full suite
1139 passing. End-to-end verified against a live instance with real provider
keys: health validation, non-streaming and streaming completions routed to
Google, cooldown listing and clearing, DB permissions, and a log scan showing
no key present.

first-run setup code, key file out of the DB, CSV export hardening (#477)

* fix(crypto): store dev-fallback encryption key in a file, not the DB it protects

When ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset outside production, the auto-generated key was
persisted into the `settings` table next to the ciphertext of provider keys, so
encryption-at-rest protected nothing for a default install: copying the DB
copied the key. Persist the key to a `.encryption-key` file next to the SQLite
database instead (derived from the resolved DB path, chmod 0600, written via
temp-file-and-rename).

Precedence: ENCRYPTION_KEY env > existing key file > legacy settings-table row
(migrated to the file with a decrypt round-trip check, then deleted) > freshly
generated key. In-memory and anonymous databases keep the settings-table
behavior since they have no directory to hold the file. Existing installs keep
decrypting their stored keys seamlessly.

Also ignore `.encryption-key` in git/docker so a generated dev key is never
committed or shipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): gate remote first-run setup behind a one-time code

POST /api/auth/setup succeeded unauthenticated while there are zero users. The
server binds all interfaces by default, so an exposed fresh install could be
claimed by whoever reached it first.

Keep local/desktop first-run frictionless but gate remote claims: at boot, when
there are no accounts, mint a random one-time setup code and log it. In the
setup route, a caller on a loopback socket may create the first account without
the code (validated against req.socket.remoteAddress, not req.ip or
X-Forwarded-For, which are spoofable behind a proxy). A non-loopback caller must
supply a matching setupCode or gets a 403 with a machine-readable
`setup_code_required` type. The code is regenerated each boot and cleared once
an account exists.

Surface the requirement in the dashboard: apiFetch now carries the HTTP status
and error type on the thrown error, and the setup form reveals a setup-code
field only after a `setup_code_required` 403.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(keys): neutralize CSV formula injection in key export

The CSV export's escCsv helper only doubled quotes, so a key label like
`=HYPERLINK(...)` stayed a live formula when the file was opened in Excel or
Sheets. Prefix any cell that starts with =, +, -, @, tab or CR with a single
quote so spreadsheets read it as text. Applied only to the user-controlled label
field; the key value must round-trip verbatim for re-import and the platform is
one of our own fixed enum values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="P1 remainder: cooldown-probe recovery, client AbortSignal propagation, honest exhaustion statuses (#601)

* Cooldown-probe recovery: clear pessimistic benches early when the key validates

Cooldowns are deliberately pessimistic (90s transient, escalation ladder up
to a day, 5-minute auth bench), so capacity sits idle after the provider has
actually recovered. A new background job probes keys sitting in a cooldown
with the same cheap validateKey call the health checker uses, and clears the
bench early when the probe passes.

- Cooldown provenance: setCooldown now records WHY the bench exists
  ('heuristic' | 'authoritative' | 'credit' | 'tier', plus set_at_ms) via a
  new migration on rate_limit_cooldowns. Only heuristic benches — our own
  guesses — are ever probed; Retry-After-backed and daily-reset expiries are
  provider-stated facts, and 402/403 benches cannot be disproven by a key
  validation, so all of those are filtered out at the query.
- Probe discipline: per-key unit (one validate covers every model benched on
  that key), ripeness gate (no probe before half the bench has elapsed or
  when it expires within a scan anyway), exponential per-key backoff on
  failure (2m -> 15m cap), jittered first probe so a restart cannot
  thundering-herd providers, and a per-pass probe budget
  (COOLDOWN_PROBE_MAX_PER_PASS, default 3). A failed probe never touches the
  bench, and probeKeyValidity is side-effect-free by design so probes cannot
  feed the health checker's auto-disable counter.
- Kill switch: COOLDOWN_PROBE_DISABLED=1, same convention as
  CATALOG_SYNC_DISABLED.

Mined from the Naster17/freellmapi-pro fork's recovery-probe idea, rebuilt on
the PR #597 cooldown surface instead of a parallel store.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Thread client AbortSignal through provider fetch, body reads, and streams

fetchWithTimeout bounded only time-to-headers: the abort timer was cleared
the moment headers arrived, so a hung body read stalled res.json() forever,
and a client disconnect never canceled the in-flight upstream request —
tokens kept burning and the in-flight lease stayed held until the read
happened to finish. (P1, mined from the frankljlyy-ai and MLuqmanBR forks.)

- CompletionOptions.signal: every proxy surface (/completions,
  /chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/messages) now arms an
  AbortController on res 'close' (writableEnded distinguishes a real
  disconnect) and threads its signal into the provider call.
- fetchWithTimeout composes that signal with the per-attempt timeout via
  AbortSignal.any. The timeout keeps its historical header-only scope for
  streams ('headers' bounds, disarmed at headers; the stall watchdog +
  client signal own the body), and gains whole-request scope for
  non-streaming calls ('request' bounds, timer left armed across the body
  read and unref'd) so a hung body read now aborts at the deadline.
- newClientAbortError / isClientAbortError (lib/error-classify.ts): the
  client abort carries a structured marker; undici propagates the reason
  through fetch, res.json(), and reader.read() rejections. The fallback
  loop stops the ladder on it immediately — no cooldown, no health
  penalty, no failure stats, no error log row, nothing rendered (the
  socket is gone) — while the finally still frees the in-flight lease.
  socksFetch preserves the marked reason instead of minting a generic
  tagged AbortError.
- google.ts's hand-rolled Gemini stream reader gains the same
  PROVIDER_STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS inactivity watchdog as readSseStream
  (shared readWithStallTimeout helper in base.ts); its reads were
  previously unbounded.
- openai-compat rethrows abort-like body-read rejections instead of
  misdiagnosing them as a non-OpenAI-compatible endpoint body.

Covered fetch sites: all 14 fetchWithTimeout call sites across
openai-compat/google/cohere/cloudflare/aihorde (chat + stream + validate).
Skipped: google.ts imageUrlToInlineData (already bounded by its own 30s
AbortSignal.timeout; no options in scope).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Honest exhaustion statuses: failure-kind -> terminal-status taxonomy

When the fallback ladder exhausted every candidate, everything collapsed
into a generic 429 "All models rate-limited" (or an opaque routing_error),
hiding WHY the request failed and when a retry could succeed. The single
exhaustion seam (exhaustedRetryError in lib/fallback-loop.ts) now
aggregates the per-attempt failure kinds and renders the honest terminal
status on every surface (chat/completions, legacy completions,
/v1/responses, /v1/messages):

- every attempt context/prompt-too-large -> 413 context_length_exceeded
  (new isContextTooLargeError classifier covering OpenAI-compat
  "maximum context length"/context_length_exceeded, Anthropic "prompt is
  too long", Google "input token count ... exceeds", Groq TPM-ceiling
  413s, and generic payload-too-large gateways)
- every candidate unavailable-until-known-time (rate limits, benched
  daily quotas, out-of-credits, tier-forbidden) -> 429 with retryAtMs
  (soonest cooldown expiry, epoch ms) in the error body and a matching
  Retry-After header (seconds, ceil)
- every attempt model-not-found/gone upstream -> 404 model_not_found
  (no 410: the catalog keeps no removal tombstones, so "verifiably
  existed and was removed" is not determinable)
- zero-attempt routing exhaustion now maps diagnostics through the same
  taxonomy (routingExhaustionBody): nothing configured -> 503
  no_providers_configured; all candidates too small -> 413; candidates
  merely cooling down -> 429 + retryAtMs
- mixed/other upstream failures (5xx, timeouts, transport) -> 502
  upstream_failed: the upstream failed, not the client (and not a 500,
  which stays reserved for our own bugs); a rate-limit + upstream mix
  prefers 502 because waiting is not a promise there
- explicit unknown/disabled model pre-checks -> honest 404 (OpenAI
  semantics); a unified group with providers but no enabled key -> 503

All exhaustion bodies now carry a machine-readable code (and retryAtMs
where applicable) via a shared exhaustionErrorPayload/
setExhaustionHeaders pair, so the OpenAI-compatible error shape cannot
drift between surfaces; the Anthropic surface remaps kinds onto its own
vocabulary (request_too_large, not_found_error, api_error). Existing
precedence is preserved: all-auth 502 and unanimous aggregates outrank
the circuit-breaker 503, which outranks the 429/502 split.

Mined from the RObotiaga, Naster17 and frankljlyy-ai forks (P1).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gitignore: cover runtime data/ at repo root

Same contents as server/data (SQLite DB + auto-generated encryption
keyfile) when the server is launched from the repo root — same rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="Initial release of FreeLLMAPI

Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible proxy that aggregates the free tiers of
fourteen LLM providers — Google, Groq, Cerebras, SambaNova, NVIDIA,
Mistral, OpenRouter, GitHub Models, Hugging Face, Cohere, Cloudflare,
Zhipu, Moonshot, MiniMax — behind a single /v1/chat/completions endpoint.

Server:
- Express + SQLite, per-provider adapters with streaming and non-streaming
  support, automatic fallover on 429/5xx, per-key RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD tracking,
  sticky sessions for multi-turn, AES-256-GCM encrypted key storage,
  unified bearer-token auth, periodic health checks.

Client:
- React + Vite + shadcn/ui admin dashboard: keys, fallback chain (drag
  to reorder, color-coded per-provider monthly token budget), playground,
  analytics with per-provider breakdowns.

Tooling:
- GitHub Actions CI (server tests + client build), MIT license,
  README with provider-by-provider ToS review.

For personal experimentation, not production." class="Link--secondary" href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/commit/04e15037f24798b64c62df8f8bd8832df2fdcf6b">Initial release of <p dir="auto"><strong>4 billion tokens per month.  28 free LLM providers. 339 free model endpoints. One OpenAI-compatible endpoint.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Aggregate free tiers from dozens of providers, plus custom OpenAI-compatible chat, embedding, image, and audio endpoints, behind a single <code>/v1</code> API. Keys are stored encrypted. A router picks the best available model for each request, falls over to the next provider when one is rate-limited, and tracks per-key usage so you stay under every free-tier cap.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why this exists</h2><a id="user-content-why-this-exists" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why this exists" href="#why-this-exists"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Every serious AI lab now offers a free tier, a few million tokens a month, a few thousand requests a day. On its own each tier is a toy. Stacked together, they add up to roughly <strong>4 billion tokens per month</strong> of working inference capacity, across <strong>235 model families / 339 provider endpoints</strong> from small-and-fast to reasonably capable.</p>
<p dir="auto">The problem is that stacking them by hand is painful: twenty-eight different SDKs, twenty-eight different rate limits, twenty-eight places a request can fail. FreeLLMAPI collapses that into one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Point any OpenAI client library at your local server, and it routes transparently across whichever providers you've added keys for.</p>
<p dir="auto">And the free-tier landscape shifts weekly: providers launch models, retire them, and change quotas without notice. FreeLLMAPI tracks all of that for you. The router pulls a signed model catalog from <a href="https://freellmapi.co" rel="nofollow">freellmapi.co</a> on its own, so your install keeps up without a <code>git pull</code>. See <a href="#premium-live-catalog">Premium (live catalog)</a> for how fast it keeps up.</p>

<p dir="auto">Most of these configure themselves with one command — <code>npx freellmapi setup-claude</code>, <code>setup-codex</code>, <code>setup-aider</code>, and ten more generators that fetch your live catalog, back up existing config, and never clobber what's already there. Claude Code and Codex also get zero-persistence launchers (<code>freellmapi launch</code>, <code>freellmapi launch-codex</code>) that inject credentials into the child process only. Zed and JetBrains AI connect through the opt-in <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/clients.md#ollama-clients">Ollama emulation</a>; Gemini CLI speaks its native wire on <code>/v1beta</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Per-tool recipes, the setup CLI reference, revocable URL tokens for headerless clients, and the MCP server all live in <strong><a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/clients.md">Clients & coding agents →</a></strong></p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Features</h2><a id="user-content-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Features" href="#features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/repo-assets/features.png"><img src="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/raw/main/repo-assets/features.png" alt="Feature overview" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Every OpenAI surface</strong> — <code>/v1/chat/completions</code>, <code>/v1/responses</code> (what Codex CLI needs), <code>/v1/completions</code> (editor ghost-text autocomplete), <code>/v1/images/generations</code>, <code>/v1/audio/speech</code>, <code>/v1/embeddings</code>, and <code>/v1/models</code> — streaming and non-streaming, from the official SDKs or any OpenAI-compatible client. <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/api.md">API reference →</a></li>
<li><strong>Anthropic Messages API</strong> — <code>/v1/messages</code> speaks Anthropic's wire format over the same router, so <strong>Claude Code</strong> and the official Anthropic SDKs run against your free pool. <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/api.md#anthropic--claude-clients">Details →</a></li>
<li><strong>Native Gemini + Ollama surfaces</strong> — Gemini CLI can use <code>/v1beta</code> (<code>generateContent</code>, streaming, token counting, models), while opt-in Ollama emulation serves NDJSON chat/generate, tags, metadata, and embeddings for Zed, JetBrains, and other local-model clients.</li>
<li><strong>Fusion (multi-model synthesis)</strong> — request the virtual <code>fusion</code> model and the router fans your prompt out to a panel of diverse free models in parallel, then a judge model synthesizes one answer from the drafts. <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/api.md#fusion-multi-model-synthesis">Details →</a></li>
<li><strong>Image generation & text-to-speech</strong> — <code>/v1/images/generations</code> and <code>/v1/audio/speech</code> route across the providers that serve media models, including custom OpenAI-compatible media endpoints.</li>
<li><strong>Tool calling & structured outputs</strong> — OpenAI-style <code>tools</code> round-trip across providers (plain-text tool calls are rescued into real <code>tool_calls</code>), plus <code>response_format</code>, <code>seed</code>, <code>logprobs</code>, penalties, and the rest of the sampling params passed through per provider.</li>
<li><strong>Smart routing, six strategies</strong> — live per-model speed/capability/reliability scores rank your chain; automatic fallover retries the next model on 429/5xx with cooldowns and key rotation. <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#routing-in-detail">Routing in detail →</a></li>
<li><strong>Unified models & profiles</strong> — the same model on several providers collapses into one entry with strict in-group failover; named fallback-chain profiles (a coding chain, a vision chain) switch from the dashboard or per request via <code>auto:<profile></code>.</li>
<li><strong>Per-key rate tracking</strong> — RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD counters per <code>(platform, model, key)</code> that learn providers' reported ceilings, so routing always stays under every cap.</li>
<li><strong>Self-updating model catalog</strong> — the router syncs a signed catalog from freellmapi.co twice a day: new models, quota changes, and provider quirk fixes land automatically. <a href="#premium-live-catalog">Premium →</a></li>
<li><strong>Sticky sessions & context handoff</strong> — conversations stay on one model for 30 minutes; an optional compact handoff note keeps the thread coherent when a mid-chat switch does happen. <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/clients.md#context-handoff">Details →</a></li>
<li><strong>Prompt compression (opt-in)</strong> — a shared, fail-open request pipeline can deduplicate prompts, filter tool output, compact repeated JSON, and trim stale context before cache lookup and routing. <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/compression.md">Details →</a></li>
<li><strong>Encrypted keys, one token out</strong> — provider keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted in SQLite and decrypted in-memory per request; your apps only ever see a single unified <code>freellmapi-…</code> bearer token.</li>
<li><strong>Admin dashboard & analytics</strong> — React UI to manage keys, reorder the chain, run a playground, and read p50/p95/TTFT analytics over 24h–90d windows; login-gated, dark/light themes, <a href="#languages">60 languages</a>.</li>
<li><strong>MCP server & interactive docs</strong> — agents can introspect usable models, provider health, and routing strategy over <code>/mcp</code>; a dependency-free OpenAPI viewer lives at <code>/v1/docs</code>. <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/clients.md">Coding agents →</a></li>
<li><strong>Ops niceties</strong> — opt-in response cache, encrypted DB backups, periodic key health checks, bulk key import/export, declarative startup config. <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/install.md">Install & deploy →</a></li>
<li><strong>Runs anywhere Node 20+ runs</strong> — Windows, macOS, Linux servers, or a small ARM SBC (Raspberry Pi included). ~40 MB RSS at idle behind PM2 / systemd / whatever supervisor you prefer.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The scope is deliberately narrow — see <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#not-yet-supported">what's not supported yet</a>.</p>

<p dir="auto">Prefer to read before you pipe to bash? <a href="https://freellmapi.co/install.sh" rel="nofollow">The script is here</a>. Re-running it is safe: your <code>.env</code> (and encryption key) is preserved and the container updates to <code>:latest</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Open <a href="http://localhost:3001" rel="nofollow">http://localhost:3001</a>, add your provider keys on the <strong>Keys</strong> page, reorder the <strong>Fallback Chain</strong> to taste, and grab your unified API key from the <strong>Keys</strong> page header. <p dir="auto">FreeLLMAPI is local-first and single-user by design. Your provider keys stay in your SQLite database, encrypted at rest, and requests go from your machine to the upstream providers you enabled.</p>

<p dir="auto">The dashboard ships in <strong>60 languages</strong> (the desktop tray menu in 6). The UI
auto-detects your browser/system language on first load and you can switch any
time from <strong>⋯ → Settings</strong>; the choice is remembered. Right-to-left languages
(العربية, עברית, فارسی, اردو) flip the whole layout automatically, and only the
active language's dictionary is loaded — the rest never touch your bandwidth.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Premium (live catalog)</h2><a id="user-content-premium-live-catalog" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Premium (live catalog)" href="#premium-live-catalog"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The router keeps its model catalog fresh on its own: it pulls a signed catalog
from <a href="https://freellmapi.co" rel="nofollow">freellmapi.co</a> twice a day and applies new models,
quota changes, and provider quirk fixes to your local DB. Your own
enable/disable choices and custom providers are never touched, and every
download is verified against a pinned Ed25519 key before it is applied.</p>
<p dir="auto">The catalog currently tracks <strong>28 providers</strong>, <strong>235 model families</strong>, <strong>339
provider/model endpoints</strong>, and roughly <strong>4 billion tokens per month</strong> of listed
free-tier capacity. Browse the full set at
<strong><a href="https://freellmapi.co/models.html" rel="nofollow">freellmapi.co/models</a></strong>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Premium keeps that signed catalog live on every router you run. When a provider
launches a strong free model, quietly tightens a quota, or breaks a wire format,
live-feed routers receive the update as soon as we ship it.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong><a href="https://freellmapi.co/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=premium&utm_content=readme_bottom#pricing" rel="nofollow">Go live at freellmapi.co →</a></strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>$19/year or $49 once, lifetime. Stripe checkout; cancel anytime, self-serve.</li>
<li>One <code>fla_</code> key covers every router you run: desktop, homelab, Raspberry Pi.</li>
<li>Activate in the dashboard under <strong>Premium</strong>; cancel or manage billing
self-serve at <a href="https://freellmapi.co/manage" rel="nofollow">freellmapi.co/manage</a>.</li>
<li>The router itself stays MIT-licensed and fully free, forever. Premium is only
the live feed, and it's what funds the daily model testing and catalog
maintenance that keeps the catalog working.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The catalog server never sees your prompts, completions, or provider keys — the
router stays fully self-hosted either way.</p>

<p dir="auto">One request in, the best free model out: the router picks the highest-priority model with a healthy key that's under all its rate limits, decrypts the key in memory, and calls the provider — on a 429/5xx it cools that key down and retries the next model in your chain. The component walkthrough, routing internals, and operational details live in <strong><a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/architecture.md">docs/architecture.md</a></strong>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Limitations</h2><a id="user-content-limitations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Limitations" href="#limitations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Stacking free tiers has real trade-offs: no frontier models, variable latency, no SLA — and the effective intelligence of the endpoint dips late in the day as top models hit their daily caps, then resets at UTC midnight. Read the honest list in <strong><a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#limitations">docs/architecture.md#limitations</a></strong> before building anything real on this.</p>

<p dir="auto">Contributors very welcome! See <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> for the dev loop, PR expectations, and the policy on AI/LLM-assisted contributions (short version: welcome, same quality bar as any other PR). Good first PRs:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Add a provider</strong> — copy <code>server/src/providers/openai-compat.ts</code> as a template, wire it into <code>server/src/providers/index.ts</code>, seed its models in <code>server/src/db/index.ts</code>, add a test in <code>server/src/__tests__/providers/</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Add an endpoint</strong> — moderations and other OpenAI-compatible surfaces. The provider base class can grow new methods; adapters declare which they support.</li>
<li><strong>Improve the router</strong> — cost-aware routing (cheapest-healthy-fastest tradeoffs), better latency-weighted priority, regional pinning.</li>
<li><strong>Dashboard polish</strong> — charts on the Analytics page, key rotation UX, batch import of keys from <code>.env</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Docs</strong> — more examples, client library snippets for Go/Rust/etc., a deployment recipe for Docker or Fly.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><code>npm install && npm run dev</code> gets you the server on :3001 and the dashboard on :5173, both with HMR. PRs should include a test, keep the existing suite green (<code>npm test</code>), and match the <code>.editorconfig</code> / tsconfig defaults already in the repo. Database migration workflow and the full contributor loop are in <a href="/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a>.</p>
